scenario: [LINT.7.2] makes an interval valid when `start <= end`, so an empty one, `start == end`, is valid ([LINT.7.1]) and contains nothing. One S with `t`, `a` and `b` all 5: rule `inside`, testing `s.t in (s.a .. s.b)`, does not fire, because the half-open `[5, 5)` holds no point, and raises no fault, so rule `handler` never fires. Rule `seen` fires on the fact and logs `seen 1`, so the vector cannot pass with nothing run. A check written `start < end` would raise DOMAIN here and `handler` would log. PATH PINNED: FN_INTERVAL_CHECK's pair test `s <= e` accepting equality, in libds `eval_interval_check` (rete/eval.c) and Mercury `ds.eval.rlow_6_1_7_interval_check`.
rules_ds:
schema S scope logical:
    id: Int key
    t: Int mutable
    a: Int mutable
    b: Int mutable

rule inside:
    S s where s.t in (s.a .. s.b)
->
    log info "inside {s.id}"

rule seen:
    S s
->
    log info "seen {s.id}"

rule handler:
    ComputationError e
->
    log critical "{e.kind} [{e.schema}] [{e.slot}]"
